description: Single-panel line chart, no sub-panels. x-axis: annealing temperature, labelled T(°C), ticks every 50 °C from 750 to 1050; y-axis: tensile strength, labelled TS (MPa), gridlines every 20 MPa from 630 to 830. Nine marker-and-line curves are plotted, colour-coded by Al level: green = 6Al (diamonds), red = 6Al+XSi (squares), dark blue = 7Al (triangles); legend entries are "6Al 1min", "6Al 136sec", "6Al 5min", "6Al+XSi 1min", "6Al+XSi 136sec", "6Al+XSi 5min", "7Al 1min", "7Al 136sec", "7Al 5min". Data points lie near 800, 850, 900, ≈965 and 1000 °C. The caption identifies the alloys as 8.5Mn-0.2C (wt.%) austenite-ferrite. Every curve falls with rising temperature: the 6Al+XSi series starts highest, just below the 810 MPa gridline at 800 °C, and drops steeply to about the 750 MPa gridline at 850 °C, while the 6Al series starts near 740 MPa and 7Al near 755 MPa; by 1000 °C all nine curves converge into the 650-720 MPa band. No numeric data labels are printed on any point. The figure demonstrates that tensile strength decreases with annealing temperature and, within a composition group, with longer annealing time, and that the Si-bearing 6Al composition gives the highest strengths while 7Al lies intermediate.

subfigures.description: Single line plot of tensile strength TS (MPa), y-axis 630-830 with 20 MPa gridlines, versus annealing temperature T(°C), x-axis 750-1050 with 50 °C ticks. Nine series are keyed in a boxed legend at upper right: green diamonds for 6Al at 1min, 136sec and 5min; red squares for 6Al+XSi at the same three times; dark blue triangles for 7Al at the same three times. All series decrease with temperature and converge near 650-720 MPa at 1000 °C; the 6Al+XSi series has the highest values at low temperature.

observations.observation: The figure is a single line chart of tensile strength TS (MPa) on the y-axis (gridlines 630 to 830 in 20 MPa steps) against annealing temperature T(°C) on the x-axis (ticks 750 to 1050 in 50 °C steps).
The boxed legend lists nine series: 6Al 1min, 6Al 136sec, 6Al 5min, 6Al+XSi 1min, 6Al+XSi 136sec, 6Al+XSi 5min, 7Al 1min, 7Al 136sec and 7Al 5min.
Curves are colour-grouped by composition: green symbols for 6Al, red for 6Al+XSi and dark blue for 7Al.
Tensile strength decreases with increasing annealing temperature for every one of the nine plotted series.
At 800 °C the 6Al+XSi series reaches the highest value in the chart, sitting just below the 810 MPa gridline, whereas the 7Al curves lie close to the 750 MPa gridline and the 6Al curves near 740 MPa.
The 6Al+XSi curve that starts just below 810 MPa at 800 °C drops steeply to about the 750 MPa gridline at 850 °C, the largest fall of any series over that interval.
By 1000 °C all nine curves have converged into a narrow band between the 650 and 720 MPa gridlines.
Data points are placed at approximately 800, 850, 900, ~965 and 1000 °C; no numeric value labels are printed beside any data point.

Within each colour group the three annealing times are drawn as separate curves, but the open-versus-filled marker coding that distinguishes 1min, 136sec and 5min is only partially legible at the supplied resolution, so individual time curves cannot be matched with certainty.
The caption states the alloys are a series of 8.5Mn-0.2C (wt.%) austenite-ferrite alloys (written 'austeniteferrite' in the caption).
The caption states the figure shows the influence of annealing temperature, time and composition content on tensile strength.
The citing text states that increasing the annealing temperature and/or time leads to a decrease in tensile strength, with yield strength behaving in a similar way.
The citing text states that the observed change in strength per degree (MPa/°C) for this concept is relatively small.
The citing text states that the influence of Al and Si, both important solid-solution strengtheners, is observed in this figure.
